newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-CAUTIOUS LARA BUILDS WEST INDIES' REPLY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CAUTIOUS LARA BUILDS WEST INDIES' REPLY.

text.p: Brian Lara shed his normal flamboyance as West Indies inched their way towards Australia's first innings 243 with grim determination in the fifth and final test on Sunday.
The West Indies vice-captain, who has endured a dismal series with the bat, played with unusual caution in a circumspect innings on the second morning at the WACA.
At lunch, West Indies were 84 for two after starting the day on 25 without loss.

Instead of trying to dominate the bowling from the outset, a tactic that has failed him so far in the series, Lara concentrated on defence to remain unbeaten on 15 from 58 balls in partnership with opener Robert Samuels on 29 not out.

Lara, the world record holder for the highest score in test and first class cricket, has averaged just 20 in the series and was greeted by a field of three slips and three gulleys on his arrival at the wicket against fast bowler Glenn McGrath.

McGrath earlier tempted number three Shivnarine Chanderpaul into a rash and hurried hook shot with his score on three. The ball flew straight to fine leg, where fellow fast bowler Paul Reiffel took a simple catch.
Reiffel made the initial breakthrough on Sunday by dismissing opener Sherwin Campbell for 21 with the total on 30. The right-hander edged a delivery to wicketkeeper Ian Healy.
West Indies added only 59 runs in 28 overs against a relentlessly accurate Australian attack.
Lara, who was told advised by West Indies team manager and former captain Clive Lloyd before the test to work harder for his runs, appeared to heed the advice.
Fast bowler Curtly Ambrose underlined his importance to West Indies by claiming five for 43 on Saturday on his return from injury, while Michael Bevan and Mark Waugh both scored fine half centuries.
